chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Mu'azi narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Tayalesi, from Sayf ibn Umayrah, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
'What is [the reward] for one who performs the Hajj five times?' He replied: 'One who performs the Hajj five times, God will never punish him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for performing the Hajj pilgrimage five times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the cumulative spiritual merit of repeated devotion, linking the specific act of five Hajjs to absolute exemption from divine punishment (*al-Adhab*). This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *Tawassul* through consistent worship, where the accumulation of righteous deeds serves as a shield against the consequences of sins, provided the heart remains sincere.
